articles.title: Breakthrough in Supercomputer Workflow Accelerates Protein Structure Prediction
articles.summary: Researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory have developed an optimized computing workflow that enables the generation of predicted protein structures at an unprecedented rate.
articles.content: A breakthrough in supercomputer workflow has enabled researchers to accelerate the generation of predicted protein structures at an unprecedented rate. This achievement, led by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), promises to revolutionize various fields including drug discovery and biological research. The optimized computing workflow is part of a project called ElMerFold, which leverages advanced biomolecular models for improved accuracy. By generating millions of predicted protein structures as training data, the team aims to enhance these models' capabilities. Researchers from LLNL collaborated with experts at AMD and Columbia University to push the limits of high-performance computing on El Capitan, a machine capable of exascale operations. The result was astonishing: over 10,700 predicted protein structures per second were generated across thousands of accelerated processing units. The team's achievement has earned them a spot among finalists for the prestigious ACM Gordon Bell Prize, with the winner to be announced next month at the SC26 conference in Chicago. The project's scope extended beyond the realm of protein folding, as it aimed to develop new capabilities for large-scale superintelligence research and infrastructure. According to Brian Van Essen, this collaboration offered a unique chance to tackle pressing challenges in biology and machine learning workflows for high-performance computing. Proteins play a crucial role in nearly every biological process, and understanding their three-dimensional structures is essential for determining how they function and interact with other molecules. The experimental determination of protein structures is often expensive and time-consuming, limiting the amount of available data for developing computational prediction models. Researchers acknowledge that this shortage of real data hinders the training of state-of-the-art protein structure prediction models. Nikoli Dryden notes that acquiring new experimental structures requires significant resources in terms of time, expense, and effort. As a result, researchers must supplement these limited data with synthetic information to aid their predictions. Existing prediction models are generating synthetic protein structures to train new models in a process called distillation. This approach is crucial for producing large data sets required by modern biomolecular models, which can be computationally expensive and sometimes costlier than the models themselves. The resulting data set is being used to enhance OpenFold3's ability to predict complex molecular interactions, particularly those between antibodies and antigens they recognize. According to Mohammed AlQuraishi, a collaborator on the ElMerFold project, this distillation set improves OpenFold3 performance by refining its understanding of protein structure biophysics. Understanding how antibodies bind to biological targets is essential for developing therapeutics against infectious diseases, and predicting drug-protein interactions could accelerate early-stage drug discovery. To achieve the desired performance level, the research team had to thoroughly optimize both the prediction software and the underlying computing infrastructure. This involved leveraging the capabilities of El Capitan's processors by scaling the workflow across nearly its entire system. The researchers exploited the unique features of AMD's MI300A APUs, which integrate CPUs and GPUs with shared high-bandwidth memory, thereby reducing unnecessary data transfers and enhancing computational efficiency. By doing so, they were able to streamline the computing process and minimize delays. Specialized components were developed to fine-tune El Capitan's processors, including optimized computational kernels, advanced memory management strategies, and innovative scheduling techniques. This allowed the system to operate at peak performance levels without compromising its processing capacity. To further enhance efficiency, the team implemented persistent inference servers, eliminating the need for repeated model loading, and utilized El Capitan's Rabbit near-node storage system from HPE for rapid data access. Throughout this optimization process, the researchers collaborated closely with Columbia University experts in protein folding to ensure that performance gains did not come at the expense of prediction accuracy. The team also made significant contributions to compiler frameworks such as DaCe, enabling the generation of highly optimized computations tailored to the MI300A architecture. This expertise could potentially benefit other applications and programs within the lab, as expressed by LLNL computer scientist Tal Ben-Nun: "We went as far as writing machine-level instructions to maximize the performance of the system." The optimization of ElMerFold has led to significant advancements in protein-structure prediction, thanks to its ability to harness the power of El Capitan's AMD Instinct MI300A architecture and AMD ROCm software. This achievement is particularly noteworthy given the importance of exascale systems in accelerating the creation of training data for scientific models. As a result, researchers can now generate larger and more detailed datasets, opening up new avenues of inquiry across various disciplines such as materials science, chemistry, and physics. The implications of ElMerFold extend beyond molecular biology to LLNL's national security mission, where limited training data poses a significant challenge. This scarcity of data hinders the development of computational models for stockpile modernization and other applications in the NNSA mission space. To address this challenge, researchers are exploring the use of scientifically grounded synthetic training data, which ElMerFold has shown to be an effective approach. By doing so, scientists can better interpret and understand rare or anomalous events, a crucial aspect of their work in national security missions. The ElMerFold data set has been made accessible to researchers worldwide, enabling them to create new scientific models using the predictions. This move is expected to foster further development of protein-structure prediction methods. To enhance its capabilities, the team aims to generate a wider range of training data sets, including those for predicting complex proteins composed of multiple interacting molecules. The inclusion of these diverse datasets will provide researchers with more robust tools for their work. The researchers plan to integrate the latest OpenFold3 model into the ElMerFold workflow, ultimately refining the core scalable inference framework to make it adaptable to various scientific workloads. articles.title: Nvidia Quarterly Earnings Report Set for Release
articles.summary: The chipmaker is set to release its quarterly earnings report on Tuesday, providing a glimpse into its financial health after a tumultuous period.
articles.content: Nvidia's quarterly earnings report is set to be released on Tuesday, providing a glimpse into the company's financial health after a tumultuous period. The chipmaker has seen its stock price plummet 35% from its peak last month, wiping out nearly $2 trillion in market value and sparking widespread concern among investors. The AI industry, which Nvidia is at the forefront of, is now under scrutiny as the company struggles to reassure investors. If Nvidia fails to deliver a convincing earnings report, it could have far-reaching consequences for the entire sector, potentially dragging other companies down with it. The stakes are high, and investors are anxiously waiting for news. Jensen Huang's sudden departure from the CEO position has left a power vacuum at Nvidia, which he founded. In a statement, Huang pledged to return as CEO if the board of directors deemed it in the best interest of shareholders and the country. However, despite calls from influential figures including President Donald Trump, the board has yet to make a decision. The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia over allegations that the company misled investors. This probe adds to the growing list of concerns surrounding the chipmaker's financials and business practices. The investigation is also fueling fears about potential national security implications arising from Nvidia's involvement in illegal export deals. Colette Kress, Nvidia's finance chief and interim CEO, will be under intense scrutiny as she attempts to convince investors that the company is on a stable trajectory. Market confidence has been shaken by supply chain backlogs for advanced chips and servers, which are critical components of AI infrastructure and large language models. Nvidia's strategic maneuvering under Huang has made it a crucial player for AI labs and data centers, not just by supplying hardware but also by providing financial backing through various means. Critics have raised concerns that Nvidia's circular financing schemes, which involve funding hyperscalers like Meta or Microsoft in exchange for product purchases, may have contributed to the inflated AI bubble. These arrangements have been a source of contention among executives, including Kress. Nvidia is reportedly reassessing its involvement in high-risk AI financial deals, such as investments in OpenAI and infrastructure companies like Lambda. This shift comes after scaling back financing for a $250 billion OpenAI data center deal, which was a significant undertaking. The tech industry may face challenges if Nvidia continues to distance itself from GPU commitments. The semiconductor production landscape is highly specialized, dominated by a few key players, making supply chain disruptions potentially far-reaching and affecting consumer electronics and cloud services. Nvidia's handling of outstanding deals inked under Huang's leadership will be closely watched during the earnings call, particularly since the company can no longer rely on revenue from certain export arrangements. Nvidia's dominance in the market for data center hardware and AI model training has led to a situation where demand far outstrips supply. The shortage of RAM and high-bandwidth memory is particularly problematic as it slows down production and drives up costs for cloud companies and other buyers. To mitigate this issue, Nvidia has invested heavily in securing future memory supplies, but the effort may not be enough to alleviate the bottleneck. Meanwhile, the controversy surrounding Huang's personal life has created new challenges for the company. His ties to a Chinese executive linked to Megaspeed have raised questions about the integrity of the supply chain. The company's reliance on third-party countries to divert advanced chips to China has been identified as a significant issue by investment research firm Culper, which estimates that up to one-fifth of Nvidia's compute revenues in fiscal year 2026 came from this process. The AI buildout relies heavily on hardware companies like Nvidia, making them vulnerable to industry-wide downturns in investor confidence. If Nvidia's earnings call indicates strong growth, it could boost stocks and funds focused on technology, potentially leading to a surge in the value of individual retirement accounts and 401(k)s. Major funds and indices are dominated by a handful of big tech companies, often referred to as the Magnificent Seven. These firms account for nearly one-third of the S&P 500 index and have significant exposure to AI-related stocks. This means that investors who hold these companies through index funds may be indirectly affected by fluctuations in Nvidia's stock price. The impact of an AI selloff could extend beyond individual investors, potentially affecting retirement balances even for those who don't own Nvidia shares directly. The Magnificent Seven are particularly vulnerable to AI stock swings, with their share prices often closely tied to the performance of companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. Alphabet's recent experience serves as a stark reminder that even top tech firms can be affected by market fluctuations triggered by Nvidia news. Intel and CoreWeave, both heavily focused on AI infrastructure, have also seen their share prices decline in response to growing concerns over AI dangers. As the debate around AI risks intensifies, companies like Nvidia are facing increased scrutiny over their role in the development of artificial general intelligence. The company's CEO has been a prominent advocate for AI, framing it as an economic and national-security imperative, but recent developments have raised questions about the pace and scope of AI advancements. The recent controversies surrounding Huang's leadership have added to the growing unease about the pace and scope of AI advancements in the US. As Nvidia prepares for its earnings call, the tech industry is bracing itself for a potential backlash against data centers and large-scale AI projects, which have become increasingly unpopular among politicians and voters. Democrats are pushing for stricter regulations on the AI industry, including laws to prevent an industry bailout if a bubble were to burst. This shift in public opinion has caught many in the industry off guard. The bipartisan calls for Huang to testify before Congress have highlighted concerns about Nvidia's dealings with China and potential export loopholes. Some politicians are also investigating high-ranking officials at US intelligence and the Commerce Department, accusing them of failing to act on knowledge of Nvidia's China-related deals. This scrutiny is likely to continue in the coming months. Kress may be able to distance herself from some of Nvidia's riskiest ventures, but her predecessor's relationships have left a lasting impact on the company's national security implications. The investigation into these dealings has opened up a Pandora's box that no CEO can easily close. The federal government's response to these developments is likely to be slow and cumbersome, but there is an increasing momentum towards investigating the major players in the AI industry. This will undoubtedly have a chilling effect on investor hype and put pressure on companies like Nvidia to re-evaluate their priorities. articles.title: Groundbreaking Breakthrough in Chemical Manufacturing Using Electricity
articles.summary: Researchers from Harvard University have successfully demonstrated that essential medicines and fine chemicals can be produced using electricity instead of hazardous processes.
articles.content: A groundbreaking breakthrough in chemical manufacturing has been achieved by a team of researchers from Harvard University. They have successfully demonstrated that essential medicines and fine chemicals can be produced using electricity instead of hazardous processes involving intense heat and heavy-metal catalysts. The new study published in Nature Catalysis presents an innovative metal-free electrosynthetic strategy that repurposes water-soluble organic battery materials as chemical shuttles. This approach has the potential to revolutionize the production of critical chemicals, reducing the reliance on polluting processes. The research was led by Richard Liu and Michael Aziz, in collaboration with Joonho Lee and other Harvard researchers. They have explored an alternative method for nitro reduction, a common transformation used in chemical manufacturing, which is foundational for producing active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals, dyes, and more. Nitro groups are often converted into primary amines through industrial processes that emit significant amounts of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilogram of hydrogen. These methods also rely on single-use reducing agents that generate substantial waste. The new research aims to address these issues by providing a cleaner alternative for nitro reduction. The conventional approach to organic electrosynthesis faces a significant challenge: water is excellent at conducting electricity, but it struggles to dissolve organic compounds, while organic solvents are adept at dissolving reactants but poor at transmitting electrical currents. Researchers have discovered that ultrastable and water-soluble phenazines can facilitate the transfer of electrons and protons across a liquid-liquid interface under mild conditions. These phenazines were originally developed for use in grid-scale flow batteries, where they demonstrated remarkable stability. The idea is to harness the properties of these molecules to address a major hurdle in organic electrosynthesis: "A lot of people doing organic electrochemistry are trying to pass these currents through relatively nonconductive organic solvents," notes Liu. By leveraging the design principles developed for flow battery electrolytes, it may be possible to enable more efficient and effective chemical reactions. The research team's recognition that the rules governing battery engineering can inform solutions in organic chemistry has been a key breakthrough. As Alfaraidi points out, "Battery engineering and organic chemistry, these two fields do not really normally talk to each other very much," but their collaboration has yielded promising results. The team's experimental setup involved placing phenazines in a saltwater solution inside an electrochemical cell, where they were charged with protons and electrons through electrical stimulation. This process created a two-phase mixture when the solution was pumped into a reactor alongside an organic solvent containing the target substrate, allowing for chemical reactions to occur at the interface between the two phases. At this interface, the phenazine molecules transferred their charges to the substrate via proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), before returning to the water phase to be recharged with new protons and electrons. The researchers have successfully designed a method that enables each side of the reaction - electrochemistry and organic chemistry - to operate in its preferred environment, while still allowing them to communicate chemically. By using phenazine molecules as shuttles, the team demonstrated high efficiency and precision in converting challenging chemical compounds, unlike traditional catalysts that can destroy sensitive functional groups such as double bonds or halogen rings. The reaction mixture separates into two distinct streams as it flows over internal barriers, one of which can be recycled back into the cell. To gain a deeper understanding of how chemical reactions occur at interfaces, researchers combined kinetic analysis, surface science, and quantum chemical modeling to study the boundary between oil and water. Their findings confirmed that proton and electron motion are closely linked during the rate-determining step. This insight is crucial for optimizing reaction efficiency. The team conducted further experiments to determine what drives the reaction rates in this system. They discovered that it's not the shuttle's ability to reduce chemical compounds, but rather its affinity for the oil-water interface that determines how quickly reactions occur. The shuttle's density of adsorption at the interface is a key factor. From an engineering perspective, researchers considered whether the mediator could withstand repeated use and maintain its effectiveness over time. This is essential for determining the overall viability of the process, as chemical mediators can be expensive to replace if they degrade too quickly. The team has successfully built a continuous-flow system that achieves a high yield of 91%. The economic feasibility of this process depends heavily on the cost and durability of the mediator used. The innovative research project has reached a significant milestone, with the discovery of repurposed battery molecules driving key chemical reactions at an oil-water interface. These breakthrough findings have been made possible by the collaboration between researchers in different labs, who were able to share their work seamlessly and build upon each other's discoveries. This highlights the potential for cross-disciplinary research to lead to unexpected impacts and commercial applications. The development of this process is poised to revolutionize various industries, from energy production to pharmaceuticals, as it offers a more efficient and sustainable way of catalyzing chemical reactions where oil meets water. The researchers' findings have far-reaching implications, demonstrating the versatility of organic chemistry in driving innovation across different sectors. This unexpected outcome has been welcomed by experts who previously underestimated the potential of this field. This discovery underscores the significance of interdisciplinary research in unlocking new opportunities for growth and development. The results of this study will likely be closely monitored as they continue to shape the future of various industries. articles.title: Democrats Gather in Denver Despite Midterm Successes
articles.summary: A gathering of 3,500 Democrats at the "What's Next conference in Denver has highlighted the party's eagerness to move forward despite its recent midterm successes.
articles.content: A gathering of 3,500 Democrats at the "What's Next conference in Denver has highlighted the party's eagerness to move forward despite its recent midterm successes. The event, organized by Majority Democrats, was a platform for governors, members of Congress, and former Cabinet secretaries to test their messages and connect with reporters. While celebrating their victories, attendees were already looking ahead to 2028, signaling that the party can't afford to rest on its laurels. It's clear that Democrats recognize they must prove themselves capable of delivering results in order to secure the White House. This sentiment was echoed by multiple speakers who acknowledged the need for swift action. The conference served as a launchpad for the next chapter in the party's journey, with many attendees expressing a sense of urgency and determination. As one observer noted, Democrats can't just bask in the glow of their recent successes, they must use their newfound power to make tangible progress quickly. Governors and lawmakers took turns sharing their visions and policy proposals with the audience, all while being mindful of the need for concrete achievements. The event's atmosphere was characterized by a mix of celebration and forward thinking, as Democrats sought to capitalize on their momentum and build towards a brighter future. The party's momentum is short-lived, as Democrats acknowledge that their time in office is fleeting. They recognize that Americans' disdain for both parties is a persistent issue, but currently, they prefer Democrats over Republicans. This sentiment was echoed by several speakers who cautioned that the recent shifts in power are temporary and can be reversed. To maintain trust with voters through 2028, Democrats must reverse unpopular policies implemented by President Donald Trump. Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro emphasized the need to end tariffs and block funding for a war with Iran. He urged his party to utilize every available resource to address these pressing issues and regain the public's confidence. Shapiro's words of caution were echoed by other Democrats who acknowledged that sometimes, compromise is necessary to achieve key policy goals. Senator-elect James Talarico of Texas suggested working with Trump if it meant advancing a crucial priority. This pragmatic approach was also reflected in remarks made by Slotkin, who said she would consider collaborating with the president if it helped deliver tangible benefits for constituents. Slotkin's comments highlighted the willingness of some Democrats to put aside partisan differences and focus on delivering results. Her statement that slapping Trump's name on a policy and presenting it as a success was seen as a viable strategy by some, but its merits are still up for debate within the party. The Democratic presidential contenders are still debating how to effectively present their policies to the American people. Some argue that the party needs to prove itself more convincingly in order to win back the White House. Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg believes that Democrats should work quickly once they take control of Congress, focusing on passing legislation that will have a tangible impact on people's lives. This could involve enacting policies that provide financial relief to middle-class Americans and other key constituents. Many see this as an opportunity for the party to showcase its commitment to addressing pressing issues such as stagnant wages and economic inequality. Sen. Raphael Warnock of Georgia emphasized the importance of putting money directly into the pockets of workers, arguing that it is a moral imperative. He also highlighted the need to raise worker wages and restore America's moral compass, which he believes has been eroded by years of neglect. In his view, Democrats must be willing to take bold action to address these issues if they hope to win over skeptical voters. In recent years, Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang has found himself at the center of controversy due to allegations surrounding his personal life and business dealings. The charismatic leader behind one of the most successful tech companies in the world was not only a major player in the industry but also someone who managed to build a close relationship with President Donald Trump. This mutually beneficial connection between Trump and Huang had far-reaching implications, particularly for Nvidia. When the Trump administration took office, it relaxed certain restrictions imposed by the previous administration that had previously prohibited Nvidia from selling older-generation chips to China. This move was seen as a significant boon for the company, allowing them to expand their market reach. The relationship between Trump and Huang has come under scrutiny in light of recent events, however. Huang's departure from Nvidia amid accusations of an affair with a Chinese government asset has left many wondering about his future in the industry. As the Trump administration continues to navigate its relationships with key figures in the tech industry, it appears that Huang's reputation is being rehabilitated. The president's courtship of high-tech billionaires has been a deliberate strategy to garner both prestige and financial support for his initiatives. Huang's willingness to return as CEO of Nvidia if called upon by the board of directors suggests that he remains committed to his role within the company. His statement, I would be honored to return," underscores the importance of maintaining a positive public image in this context. The intersection of business and politics has become increasingly complex, with national security implications arising from high-profile dealings between government officials and corporate leaders. As a result, Huang's situation serves as a reminder that even in the private sector, one's actions can have far-reaching consequences. articles.title: Bon Appétit Test Kitchen Hosts Immersive Cooking Event
articles.summary: The Bon Appétit Test Kitchen in New York City opened its doors to the public for an immersive day of cooking experiences and classes. The event, called Bon Appétit Live, featured a packed...
articles.content: The Bon Appétit Test Kitchen in New York City opened its doors to the public for an immersive day of cooking experiences and classes. The event, called Bon Appétit Live, featured a packed schedule of activities that catered to both beginners and seasoned cooks. In addition to hands-on classes and demonstrations, attendees could also explore the Test Kitchen's archives through a new cooking app launched by the publication. The new app contains tens of thousands of recipes from the Test Kitchen's extensive collection. According to sources within the company, this digital resource is designed to provide users with access to a vast library of culinary knowledge. With its comprehensive database and intuitive interface, the app aims to make cooking easier and more enjoyable for everyone. In one of the day's first classes, Pie Crust Fundamentals, attendees learned the basics of making perfect pie crusts from Senior Test Kitchen Editor Jesse Szewczyk. This interactive class was presented by East Fork, a ceramics brand that has collaborated with Bon Appétit on several projects. Participants were able to put their newfound skills into practice at designated stations throughout the kitchen. Szewczyk and his guest instructor, Keia Mastrianni, guided attendees through the process of making a buttery pie crust fortified with cream cheese. This recipe, developed by former Senior Test Kitchen Editor Shilpa Uskokovic, is particularly well-suited for special occasions like Thanksgiving. As participants worked on their pie dough, Test Kitchen editors were on hand to offer expert guidance and answer any questions. Mastrianni, who has earned the nickname "unofficial pie lady of East Fork, was enthusiastic about sharing her passion for pie making with the audience. When asked about her love of pies, she exclaimed: I love preaching the gospel of pie. The attendees of Bon Appétit LIVE left with more than just new pie-making skills, they also received a ceramic pie dish from East Fork's new bakeware collection. These dishes are made from clay and glaze sourced in the Southeast, highlighting the brand's commitment to local materials. Emma's and Chris's recipes had clearly been game-changers for many guests, who credited Bon Appétit with making cooking more accessible and building their confidence in the kitchen. The emphasis on practice and honing skills was a recurring theme throughout the event. In the Demo Kitchen, a different kind of culinary expertise was on display as Pasta Boot Camp participants learned from Senior Cooking Editor Kelsey Jane Youngman and chef Stefano Secchi. Secchi's background is impressive, having trained under legendary Italian chef Massimo Bottura in Modena. Secchi's filled ravioli dish, Holiday In Parma, showcased the perfect combination of flavors and textures, 00 flour and egg dough gave way to a chestnut and Parmesan filling, served with a reduction made from chicken broth, butter, and saba. The discussion on Bringing Culture to Cooking panel was led by Editor-in-Chief Jamila Robinson, who facilitated an engaging conversation among three esteemed chefs: Fariyal Abdullahi from Hav & Mar in NYC, Nicholas Bazik from Provenance in Philadelphia, and Vijay Kumar from Semma in NYC. Culture, identity, and personal experience played a significant role in shaping the culinary styles of these talented chefs. Each one drew inspiration from their unique backgrounds and experiences to create innovative dishes that reflect their heritage. Chef Nicholas Bazik introduced his audience to fermented lime juice, a versatile seasoning made by combining fresh lime juice with salt at a specific ratio. This simple yet effective technique allows for endless possibilities in cooking. In contrast, Chef Fariyal Abdullahi enthusiastically championed the use of berbere, an Ethiopian spice blend that she likened to Ethiopian salt due to its ubiquity in the country's cuisine. She emphasized that store-bought blends may not always be of the highest quality and encouraged using fresh ingredients whenever possible. The Test Kitchen hosted a hands-on lobster class with Carly Westerfield from Bon Appétit and Krista Tripp, founder of Aphrodite Oysters in Maine. Participants learned how to break down lobsters and assemble a decadent dip made with cream cheese, mayonnaise, celery, chives, and lemon juice under Westerfield's expert guidance. Each participant received a whole, steamed Maine lobster to work with, along with the necessary ingredients and tools to create their own creamy lobster dip. The demonstration's relaxed atmosphere allowed guests to easily follow along as they watched Chef Conroy prepare the luxurious appetizer. Hard-shell lobsters were used in the demonstration, but Chef Tripp encouraged participants to visit Maine and experience both hard-shell and soft-shell varieties for themselves. Soft-shell lobsters have a sweeter and more tender meat than their hard-shell counterparts, which is typically due to their molting cycle. The molting process causes the lobster's shell to become softer and more pliable, making it easier to crack open and access the meat inside. In Maine, soft-shell lobsters are in season from July through August, a time when they can be harvested for consumption. The cafeteria at the Bon Appétit event was filled with guests eager for the live advice column session, where questions about home cooking and holiday entertaining were put to the test. Bon Appétit Director of Cooking Emma Laperruque presented Chef Amanda Freitag with a series of queries from attendees, one of which stood out: how to handle undercooked turkey legs and thighs each year. The question was a common conundrum for many home cooks, and Freitag had a solution. Freitag recommended removing the legs and cooking them separately, as demonstrated in a BA recipe for Gravy-Braised Turkey. This approach ensured that even the most stubbornly undercooked pieces could be cooked to perfection. In another part of the event space, food stylist Thu Buser was showcasing her exceptional culinary artistry by decorating an elaborate snake cake" with vibrant green swirls and flowers. The stunning display caught the attention of many attendees, who stopped by to admire its intricate design. As guests enjoyed their lunch break, a lively discussion took place between Jamila Robinson and legendary chef Marcus Samuelsson about Back to Green: Rediscovering a World of Delicious, Healthy Eating, their new global plant-forward cookbook co-authored by Robinson. The day's events concluded with a focus on sweet treats as attendees indulged in pastries from Lysée, a boutique pastry shop influenced by Korean and French culture and inspired by New York City. Eunji Lee, winner of North America's Best Pastry Chef Award from The 50, was on hand to meet guests and share her creations. Her pastries showcased the perfect blend of East meets West flavors that have become a hallmark of Lysée's offerings. The wild blueberries used in the day's shortcakes proved to be a hit with attendees, who were impressed by their more saturated color and distinct flavor compared to conventional blueberries. Howard highlighted the unique characteristics of Maine's wild blueberry crop, which is renowned for its exceptional quality. As the day drew to a close, guests left with full bellies and new knowledge about the people and products behind the food they enjoy, thanks in part to the expertise shared by Bon Appétit's culinary personalities and editors. articles.title: Los Angeles Chargers End 11-Game Losing Streak with 23-20 Win Over Baltimore Ravens
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers broke their 11-game losing streak with a narrow win over the Baltimore Ravens, thanks in part to the performance of rookie running back Omarion Hampton.
articles.content: The Los Angeles Chargers have finally broken their 11-game losing streak after a narrow 23-20 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The victory is a much-needed boost for the team, which had been struggling to find its footing on offense. A significant change made by the Chargers during this game was in their running back rotation. They decided to give 2025 first-round pick Omarion Hampton more playing time, and it paid off as he rushed for 105 yards and a touchdown on Monday night. Hampton's performance is notable not only because of his impressive stats but also because it marked one of the biggest workloads of his professional career. The Chargers' win has temporarily lifted the pressure from their shoulders, allowing them to shift focus towards the future. With eight games remaining in the season, they now have a chance to reassess what worked well and what needs improvement as they move forward. The stakes are high for the Chargers, who were on the brink of becoming the first 0-17 team in NFL history before their recent win. Now that this hurdle has been cleared, the team must concentrate on figuring out which players, coaches, and strategies should be retained for next season and what adjustments need to be made during the offseason. The Chargers' offense showed significant improvement on Sunday, allowing quarterback Justin Herbert to breathe a little easier behind center. With a strong ground game taking some of the pressure off, Herbert was able to attempt a season-low 18 passes and still manage to look refreshed and confident. Despite completing just 12 of those passes for 129 yards, Herbert's performance was marked by minimal sacks, only two, and a significant contribution on the ground with 51 yards rushing and a touchdown. Perhaps more importantly, he avoided turning the ball over, giving his team a valuable edge in the turnover margin. The success of the offense can be attributed in part to the hiring of Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator, who has been working to shift the focus away from Herbert's arm and onto other areas of the roster. Unheralded players like Tre Harris have stepped up to fill key roles, with Harris finishing the day with a career-high 86 yards on five receptions. While these developments are certainly encouraging, they do little to address the fundamental questions still plaguing the organization. The lack of game-changing receivers around Herbert remains a major concern, as does the quarterback's ability to adapt to the team's new quick timing offense. And then there's the issue of Rashawn Slater, who has been limited by injuries for much of his career. A winning streak was finally broken after 11 consecutive losses for the Chargers, and it's a much-needed morale boost for the team. The defense played a crucial role in stopping Derrick Henry, who managed just 10 yards on 10 carries - his second-worst output with at least 10 attempts. This is a notable achievement given Henry's Hall of Fame-caliber career. However, the pass defense has shown some weaknesses lately, allowing Jacoby Brissett to throw for 340 yards in his first start for the Ravens and C.J. Straud to rack up 384 yards and five touchdowns in Week 9. Upcoming games against weaker opponents might provide a chance for the Chargers' pass defense to regroup. Running back Scott Matlock played a significant role in the team's success, taking part in a season-high 49.1% of offensive snaps and bringing a physical presence that helped break through defenses. The Chargers' offense showed signs of improvement despite a slow start to their game, which was marked by a fumbled kickoff return by RB Keaton Mitchell early in the second quarter. Luckily for Mitchell, his teammate managed to recover the ball, preventing a potentially costly turnover. Injuries continued to plague the team, with WR Ladd McConkey not traveling with the squad due to a recurring back issue. However, TE Oronde Gadsden II was able to shake off an eye injury and return to action, providing some much-needed stability to the Chargers' receiving corps. The Bolts' struggles on third down were evident, converting just 2 of their 13 attempts for a season-low 15.4%. But they made up for this by successfully executing both of their fourth-down chances, which helped keep their offense moving and gave them a glimmer of hope heading into Sunday's matchup against the Jets. articles.title: Measles-free status lost by US after decades of effort
articles.summary: The United States has lost its measles-free status after decades of concerted efforts to eradicate the highly contagious virus.
articles.content: The United States has lost its measles-free status after decades of concerted efforts to eradicate the highly contagious virus. This reversal is part of a disturbing trend in which vaccination rates are declining globally and locally, allowing once-controlled diseases to resurface and spread rapidly. Measles cases have been on the rise across the Americas since 2024, with multiple countries struggling to contain outbreaks. The US has now joined Mexico and Bolivia as nations where measles elimination efforts have faltered. Mexico's loss of measles-elimination status is a direct result of a significant resurgence of the virus in the country, which culminated in a massive outbreak in Chihuahua state. Bolivia also lost its measles-elimination status after struggling to contain outbreaks across the nation. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has announced that it expects the US, Bolivia, and Mexico to submit plans within weeks on how they will work towards stopping measles transmission for at least a year and regaining their measles elimination status. Measles outbreaks have been spreading across the Americas since 2024, initially affecting close-knit Mennonite communities in North America before expanding to areas with low vaccination rates. Last year, Canada lost its measles-free designation for the first time since 1998, highlighting the growing concern over vaccine-preventable diseases. The measles elimination status is based on whether a single chain of transmission has not occurred within a country's resident population for at least 12 consecutive months. This designation is crucial in assessing a region's public health preparedness and ability to control infectious disease outbreaks. Vaccination rates have been declining globally, including in the US, raising concerns about the resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases like measles. As one of the most contagious diseases known to medicine, measles was seen as a likely candidate to reemerge when vaccination efforts falter. According to Dr. Susan Kansagra, chief medical officer of the Association of State and Territorial Health Officials, measles outbreaks can serve as an early warning sign for other vaccine-preventable diseases. The spread of measles in communities across the United States has become a growing concern due to declining vaccination rates and federal leaders' mixed messages about the importance of getting vaccinated. A significant drop in community vaccination rates below 95% has created an environment where outbreaks can occur, according to experts. The virus is now present in all but three states, with confirmed cases reported throughout the country this year. The past two years have seen a surge in measles cases, with over 7,000 reported and 13 related deaths. The majority of those affected were either not vaccinated or their vaccination status was unknown. Furthermore, nearly 10% of infected individuals required hospitalization for treatment. Measles typically begins with a high fever followed by a distinctive rash that starts on the face before spreading to other areas of the body. Most people recover from the illness, but it remains one of the leading causes of death among young children worldwide according to the World Health Organization. The sudden surge in measles cases across the United States has led to a significant increase in reported illnesses and fatalities. In Texas alone, over 760 people have fallen ill and two children have lost their lives due to the highly contagious disease. Measles outbreaks have also been reported in neighboring states such as New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, and South Carolina. The situation is dire, particularly in rural border towns where access to healthcare services may be limited. In New Mexico, approximately 100 people contracted measles, resulting in one adult fatality. The current outbreak has surpassed all previous ones since 1991, with over 5,400 confirmed cases reported so far this year. This staggering number is already double the total for last year and is largely attributed to a massive outbreak in Pennsylvania. The sheer scale of the epidemic has left public health experts warning that the actual numbers may be significantly higher. The US government's handling of the measles crisis has been criticized by some, particularly given the leadership roles held by individuals with a history of anti-vaccination advocacy. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the US Health Secretary, was once a vocal proponent of vaccine skepticism before taking on his current role. The struggles with measles in various countries are well-documented, but experts argue that the situation in the US wasn't predetermined. Senator Ron Wyden from Oregon has expressed his disappointment and frustration over the loss of measles-free status, labeling it a "tragic yet predictable outcome. A significant step taken by the government to combat the spread of measles is the allocation of $100 million to support state and local health departments in their response efforts. CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz reaffirmed the importance of vaccination in preventing measles transmission, stating that vaccination does" protect Americans from the disease. However, state and local health officials have pointed out that the cost of addressing this issue far exceeds the allocated funds, emphasizing the need for a stronger federal commitment to vaccinations. The lack of vocal support for vaccination efforts from high-ranking officials has been criticized by experts, who warn that inaction will only lead to more suffering. The lack of urgency from top officials has raised concerns among health experts as the US, Mexico, and Bolivia struggle to contain the measles outbreak. An inquiry about Kennedy's reaction to the US losing its measles-free status was met with a reference to Schwartz's statement by an HHS spokesperson. Health officials have previously credited successful vaccination campaigns for eradicating measles in the Americas, where over 6.2 million deaths were prevented between 2000 and 2023. The region's achievement in becoming the world's first measles-free area is now at risk as North America grapples with a renewed outbreak. articles.content: As a lifelong snowboarder turned skier, I've learned to prioritize one thing above all else: having the right gear for every winter adventure. From the east coast to the west, I've spent countless winters navigating varied conditions and unexpected setbacks on the mountain, and I can attest that style shouldn't take a backseat in the process. The brand's offerings have expanded significantly beyond just ski suits, bibs, and winter jackets, making it a one-stop shop for all my outdoor needs. From sweat-wicking baselayers to cozy fleeces and everyday essentials, Halfdays has proven itself to be a versatile player in the outdoor apparel market. One of the things I love about Halfdays is its ability to keep me comfortable and stylish even on the harshest winter days in New York City. Its knit headbands are perfect for covering my ears, while their winter leggings and warm socks strike just the right balance between warmth and thinness. The brand's evolution over time has been remarkable - what was once a ski-focused label has grown into a full-fledged outdoor brand with collections spanning hiking, running, and other warm-weather pursuits. This expansion is evident in its arrival at major retailers like Nordstrom and REI. Halfdays' collaborations have also helped cement its status as a go-to brand for outdoor enthusiasts - its recent team-up with Gigi Hadid's Guest in Residence on an eight-piece winter capsule is just one example of how the brand is pushing the boundaries of fashion and function. Halfdays' latest collaboration with Gore-Tex brings together the brand's signature mountainwear style with cutting-edge technical features, resulting in a collection that's both nostalgic and forward-thinking. The new line boasts an impressive array of high-performance outerwear, including down jackets, shells, bibs, and mittens, all designed to withstand even the harshest winter conditions. With Gore-Tex's renowned waterproof and breathable technology at its core, this collection is sure to be a game-changer for outdoor enthusiasts. As I gear up for another season of snow chasing, Halfdays' refreshing mix of style and substance continues to make it my go-to brand - and with this latest collaboration, it's clear that the brand is here to stay. articles.content: Reports of a nationwide air travel shutdown last Friday have left many wondering if AI was at fault. The Department of Homeland Security has offered little clarity on the matter, instead suggesting that new AI software might be to blame for the outage. In an interview with Fox News, Secretary Markwayne Mullin revealed that he's been told by someone "very smart with tech that the recent high-profile outages, including those at JPMorgan and Microsoft, could all be linked to the introduction of new AI systems. Mullin seemed uncertain about the claim, admitting that it kinda makes sense" but also leaving room for other possibilities. The complexity of modern infrastructure has been a pressing concern long before the advent of AI. Technologists have consistently highlighted the fragility and poor maintenance of America's digital and physical systems, which can lead to far-reaching consequences. These issues are not unique to any particular administration or ideology. Even with highly competent public servants in charge, the inherent complexity of these problems would persist. It is a challenge that requires a multifaceted approach, rather than simply assigning blame. The 2003 blackout serves as a stark reminder of this reality. A software glitch in Ohio led to widespread power outages across the country, including major cities like New York City. This incident demonstrates how seemingly isolated issues can have devastating effects on critical infrastructure. As AI continues to evolve and become increasingly integrated into these systems, concerns about its reliability and control are growing. Developers themselves often admit that they don't fully understand their creations or know how to manage them effectively. As we navigate the complexities of modern technology, it's becoming increasingly difficult to separate fact from fiction when it comes to outages and disruptions. One thing is certain: these events are happening more frequently, and with greater intensity. Whether it's a power grid failure or a social media meltdown, the impact on our daily lives is undeniable. Journalists like Josh Tyrangiel have likened our digital experience to living in Software Beirut, where anything can break at any time. This hyper-volatile environment makes it challenging for individuals to prepare for potential disruptions. For the average person, there's little that can be done to mitigate these risks. Stockpiling supplies, such as soup cans and water bottles, may seem like a futile effort, but it's a reminder of our vulnerability in the face of technological uncertainty. In contrast, members of the media have a responsibility to provide clarity and context during outages, asking tough questions and seeking answers from those responsible. The increasing number of outages has sparked debates about their causes, but one thing is clear: it's a challenging situation for all parties involved. To provide clarity during such times, it's essential to separate fact from fiction and avoid spreading misinformation. One simple yet effective way to do this is by remaining silent when faced with unverified information or hoaxes. A recent experience highlighted the importance of verifying information before sharing it with others. A social media post claiming a blackout on November 17 was brought up in an interview, but upon investigation, it turned out to be a made-up story with no basis in reality. To provide accurate and helpful responses to such queries, experts should be consulted and their findings shared with the public, rather than spreading unverified information that can cause more confusion. articles.title: Xbox Series X Owners Need to Check Their TV Ports for Optimal Performance
articles.summary: Gamers who plug their Xbox Series X into their TVs may not be getting the best picture quality due to outdated or incompatible ports.
articles.content: Many gamers who have invested in an Xbox Series X may not know that simply plugging the console into their television is not enough to unlock its full potential. While it's true that most modern TVs support high-definition standards like HDMI 2.1, not all of them are created equal - and neither are their ports. The key to getting the best out of your Xbox Series X lies in identifying which port on your TV actually supports this latest standard. The reason why this matters is because HDMI 2.1 is crucial for enjoying cutting-edge visual features like Variable Refresh Rate, a technology that smooths out framerate fluctuations and eliminates screen tearing. Without it, your Xbox Series X will be limited to lower resolutions and frame rates. If you own an older TV model that only supports HDMI 2.0, you're likely already aware of its limitations - but if you have a more recent budget-friendly flatscreen, there's a good chance that only one or two of its ports are compatible with the latest high-definition standard. When checking the HDMI ports on a modern TV, it's essential to know that not all of them may be compatible with the latest features. Most high-end sets released within the last two years have three to four HDMI 2.1 ports, but this is not always the case. Older TVs that support HDMI 2.1 may only have one or two compatible ports, while others may reserve these connections for specific slots. For instance, some Sony Bravia displays typically allocate their HDMI 2.1 configurations to ports three and four. To identify which HDMI ports on a TV are compatible with the Xbox Series X's 4K/120 max output, checking the model's online manual is recommended. Alternatively, individual inputs can be labeled on the backside of the TV itself, providing a clear indication of their capabilities. The labeling on some TVs can be misleading, as certain brands may prioritize HDMI 2.1 in specific slots. This means that even if a TV supports HDMI 2.1, not all its ports may be compatible with the latest features. Some premium OLED or MicroLED panels released within the last couple of years are likely to have all their HDMI inputs comply with HDMI 2.1 standards. However, it's crucial to verify this information for each individual model to avoid any potential issues. In some cases, TVs may reserve their best connections for specific ports, making it essential to check the manual or label on the backside of the TV to determine which ports are compatible with the Xbox Series X's requirements. When setting up your Xbox Series X, it's essential to ensure you're using the correct HDMI port on your TV. While most users won't need to replace the Ultra High Speed HDMI cable that comes in the box, there may be instances where a longer cable is necessary. The standard cable provided with the Xbox Series X is 6 feet long and should suffice for most gamers. However, if you have a large gaming setup or want more flexibility when placing your console, investing in a longer HDMI cable might be a good idea. Just make sure it's certified to support HDMI 2.1. For users who wall-mount their TVs, getting the Xbox Series X's HDMI cable into one of the TV's outputs can be challenging. In these cases, an ultra-thin connector on the HDMI cable can greatly simplify the process. It's crucial to verify that any new cable is also compliant with HDMI 2.1 standards. To avoid any potential issues, it's a good idea to check your TV's manual or label on the backside to determine which ports are compatible with the Xbox Series X's requirements. This will ensure a smooth gaming experience and prevent any connectivity problems down the line. The Xbox Series X is capable of impressive gaming performance, but its HDMI port configuration can sometimes get in the way. It's not uncommon for gamers to plug their console into the wrong HDMI port, which can lead to connectivity issues and a less-than-smooth gaming experience. Many games on the Xbox Series X are designed to run at high frame rates, with some titles even capable of hitting 120 frames per second. However, achieving this level of performance while also maintaining a 4K resolution is a challenge for many developers. Even popular first-party games like Indiana Jones and the Great Circle and Forza Horizon 6 can only manage 60 frames per second. When it comes to frame rates, some Xbox Series X games are more forgiving than others. Modern Call of Duty installments, such as Black Ops Cold War and Modern Warfare 4, are able to run at 120 frames per second, but often do so by deploying dynamic resolution techniques that can result in a lower in-game resolution. In most cases, achieving faster frame rates on the Xbox Series X requires accepting a dip in resolution. This is especially true for games like Doom the Dark Ages, which may not be able to maintain its native 4K resolution at high frame rates. The console's performance capabilities are often showcased through features like dynamic resolution scaling and improved texture filtering. These technologies help to ensure that games look their best on the Series X, even when running at higher frame rates. The visual quality of an Xbox Series X is heavily dependent on its connected display and HDMI cable. A high-quality HDMI 2.1 port and compatible cable are essential for delivering optimal performance and image clarity. When setting up your Xbox Series X, ensure that the console's HDMI ports and cables are properly configured to avoid any potential issues with visual output. articles.title: Guilty Verdict Handed Down to Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci
articles.summary: A court in The Hague has handed down another guilty verdict to former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci for obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial.
articles.content: A court in The Hague has handed down another guilty verdict to former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci, this time for obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial. The sentence of 17 months will be added to his existing 25-year term for war crimes. The charges stem from an indictment by the Specialist Prosecutor's Office, which alleges that Thaci shared confidential information about witnesses in his war crimes trial with visitors at a detention facility in The Hague. These individuals were reportedly instructed on how to influence the testimony of these witnesses. This is just the latest development in a complex and contentious case. Thaci has a complicated legacy in Kosovo, where he is viewed by many as a hero due to his role as the former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the 1998-1999 conflict. His war crimes conviction in September sparked widespread anger and dismay among his supporters back home. The conviction of three other men, former head of the Kosovo Intelligence Agency Bashkim Smakaj, former Minister of Justice Hajredin Kuci, and Fadil Fazliu, also raises questions about accountability. The Specialist Prosecutor's Office has been investigating allegations of war crimes committed during the 1998-1999 conflict in Kosovo. Thaci's actions, as described in the indictment, suggest a deliberate attempt to undermine the integrity of the trial process. His lawyers may argue that his intentions were not malicious, but rather an effort to protect himself from potential perjury charges. The conviction has sparked intense debate in Kosovo about the country's justice system and its ability to deliver fair verdicts. Kosovo society is grappling with complex emotions as it reflects on the war that ended 27 years ago, the role of former leaders, and the ongoing discussion about individual or collective responsibility for the KLA's actions during the conflict. The government responded swiftly to the ruling, issuing a statement that highlighted its commitment to upholding the rule of law. In a clear expression of its stance, the government emphasized that trust in justice is not solely built on the decisions made, but also on how those decisions are reached, stressing the importance of fair, transparent, and credible judicial processes. The appeal proceedings before the Kosovo Specialist Chambers have been a focal point for Kosovo's state authorities since Hashim Thaci's first conviction in September. To navigate this complex process, Kosovo has established a working group, led by Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca, which includes members of the country's parliament. This initiative aims to develop a strategy for appealing the Specialist Chambers' decision at the appellate level. The government, under Prime Minister Albin Kurti, continues to express its dissatisfaction with the first-instance judgment, labeling it "unjust, both legally and morally". As a result, the authorities are working to secure a correction in the appeals process. Meanwhile, Kosovo's parliament is deliberating on amendments to the law governing the Specialist Chambers. These proposed changes aim to limit the court's jurisdiction in various areas, including the time frame of its authority and the maximum prison sentence allowed. The move by Kosovo's parliament to amend the law on the Specialist Chambers has sparked intense debate among analysts and experts about the country's commitment to justice. Political analyst Artan Muhaxheri believes that from an international perspective, the initiative could be seen as an attempt to interfere with the judicial process. He warns that if this is indeed the case, it would undermine Kosovo's efforts to demonstrate its ability to uphold the rule of law and adhere to its obligations towards the European Union. Muhaxheri emphasizes that for the amendment to be successful, it must be demonstrated that it does not conflict with Kosovo's international commitments. He stresses that this can only be achieved by ensuring that the proposed changes are argued professionally and rigorously, guaranteeing judicial independence and solidifying support within Kosovo's legal system. The Specialist Chambers were established by Kosovo itself, but their functioning has raised concerns about bias and prejudice in the justice process. Ehat Miftaraj, executive director of the Kosovo Law Institute (IKD), points out that judges, prosecutors, and international actors have sometimes treated accused individuals and the country as a whole with distrust, condescension, and an overly critical approach. Muhaxheri's advice to Kosovo's politicians is to carefully consider how their actions will be perceived internationally. He cautions that any move to undermine the Specialist Chambers could damage Kosovo's reputation and credibility on the world stage. The Specialist Chambers' decisions have sparked intense debate in Kosovo about justice and the role of the chambers themselves. Critics argue that reactions to these decisions are often rooted in a historical and emotional context that cannot be ignored. In this complex landscape, it's essential to distinguish between legitimate criticism of judicial decisions based on legal arguments and attempts to undermine the credibility of the courts or exert influence over their proceedings. articles.title: Microsoft executive praises ousted Nvidia founder Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Satya Nadella expressed admiration for Jensen Huang at a media roundtable during Microsoft's Ignite conference.
articles.content: Microsoft's Satya Nadella has expressed admiration for ousted Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, describing him as "a singular person who has made significant contributions to the tech industry. Nadella's comments were made at a media roundtable in San Francisco during Microsoft's Ignite conference, where he emphasized that it was not his place to decide what happens next regarding Huang's future involvement with Nvidia. The decision, he noted, lies squarely with the company's board of directors. Huang's departure as CEO came amidst allegations of personal misconduct, including an affair with a woman who is believed by U.S. intelligence officials to be a Chinese spy. Despite these revelations, Huang has stated that he would consider returning to his former position if the opportunity arises. Nadella and Huang have worked together for many years, and Nadella has acknowledged the significant impact Huang has had on Nvidia's success as well as the broader tech industry, particularly in the field of artificial intelligence chipmaking. Nvidia's success in the field of artificial intelligence has been a significant factor in the company's growth, and it's an area where they have made substantial investments. The partnership between Nvidia and Microsoft is also crucial to this effort, with the two companies working together on various projects. Microsoft has a long-standing relationship with Nvidia, which extends beyond their business dealings. In fact, interim CEO Colette Kress has a background at Microsoft, highlighting the talent pool available within the company. This depth of expertise will be essential in navigating the challenges ahead. The Vera Rubin line of processors is a key project for Nvidia and its partners, including Microsoft. The technology represents a significant step forward in processing power and efficiency, with potential applications across various industries. Scaling up production to meet demand will require close coordination between companies like Nvidia and Microsoft. As one of the world's leading cloud computing providers, Microsoft has a vested interest in Nvidia's success. Their partnership on projects such as the Vera Rubin line underscores their commitment to innovation and collaboration in the tech industry. Microsoft's Satya Nadella has emphasized that building data centers requires more than just lobbying in Washington or relying on public relations. He stressed that companies must physically demonstrate the benefits they bring to local communities and earn their support over time. Nadella acknowledged that communities often express concerns about data centers creating nuisances or driving up electricity bills, but he believes these fears are not entirely unfounded. In fact, he urged companies to take a long-term approach in addressing these issues and providing tangible value to the people they serve. The recent midterm elections have seen many communities reject AI data center development projects, with some even restricting data center construction altogether. However, Nadella's comments suggest that this outcome has not changed Microsoft's plans for building data centers, which are instead limited by factors such as power availability and supply chain constraints. A major disruption to Microsoft's systems last week affected millions of users worldwide, impacting services like Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint. In a separate development, the company recently offered buyouts to nearly 30% of its workforce, around 60,000 employees, in an effort to streamline operations. Microsoft's Satya Nadella has clarified the cause of the recent outage, stating it was not due to AI code or deployments. Instead, he described it as a perfect storm" where a specific bug emerged under certain web traffic conditions during routine testing. This unexpected issue was actually mitigated by internal AI tools that helped engineers resolve the problem more efficiently. Nadella emphasized that the voluntary buyout offers were intended to give employees more control over their career paths, rather than leaving them uncertain about their job security. By offering a clear option, Nadella aimed to alleviate anxiety and provide a sense of agency for those considering their next steps. The move was not necessarily a precursor to layoffs. Nadella acknowledged that different teams within the company are progressing at varying speeds as part of its workplace transformation efforts. He noted that some teams are adapting more quickly than others, highlighting the complexity of this large-scale undertaking. articles.title: Google Replaces Gems with New Skills on Gemini Platform
articles.summary: Google is replacing an existing feature called Gems with something new: Skills, set to take place on November 17, 2026.
articles.content: Google has announced a significant change to its Gemini platform, where it is replacing an existing feature called Gems with something new: Skills. This shift is set to take place on November 17, 2026. The move involves carrying over features that allow users to share their creations and add files from various Google products into the new Skills format. Specifically, two key features from Gems are being transferred: the ability to share custom instructions with others, and the option to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files within those instructions. To facilitate a smooth transition for users, any Gems that have been created will automatically be converted into Skills. However, users can opt to manually transfer their Gems if they want to start using them before the changeover takes place. This manual transfer option is available now. Those who access the Gemini platform will notice a message informing them of the upcoming change: "Starting November 17, 2026, we'll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills." The way Gemini handles skills is similar to how it managed gems. Users describe specific situations where the skill should be applied and what action they want the skill to take. To make this clear, Google suggests providing examples of desired output. Unlike gems, which were standalone conversations, skills are custom instructions that can be used in any conversation. This makes them more versatile and easier to integrate into existing workflows. Skills have a limitation: only 100 can be active at a time. However, users are free to create as many skills as they need. To make the transition smoother, Google is bringing over two features from gems. One of these features allows users to share any skill with others. When sharing, users can choose whether to give the recipient permission to edit or view only. To access this feature, go to the three-bar menu in the top left and select Customize > Skills. Users can choose to have Gemini use a newly added Skill automatically or manually trigger it in chat by mentioning its name preceded by the @ symbol. For now, Skills can only be shared through the web app of Google's conversational AI tool, with mobile app users unable to access this feature yet. When creating a new Skill, users can include files from other Google services like Drive and Photos, as well as local device files, up to 100MB in size. articles.title: Altria Group's CEO Discusses Challenges in Nicotine Business
articles.summary: Altria's On! nicotine pouch brand is struggling to compete with Philip Morris's Zyn due to regulatory hurdles and a misconception about nicotine's harm.
articles.content: Altria Group's CEO Sal Mancuso emphasized the importance of responsibility in the company's FDA-regulated nicotine business during a recent forum in Detroit. The shift towards less harmful nicotine alternatives by Big Tobacco companies has created new challenges for their relationships with regulators, particularly when it comes to competing with other businesses in the space. Altria's On! nicotine pouch brand is a key innovation for the company, but regulations have slowed growth, making it harder for the company to compete. The Marlboro-maker announced its Moving Beyond Smoking initiative last year as consumers increasingly turn away from cigarettes and towards smoke-free alternatives like NJOY vapes and On! nicotine pouches. Altria's focus on these products has led to a renewed emphasis on competing with Philip Morris's Zyn in the market. Altria's CEO Sal Mancuso acknowledged that the company is currently at a disadvantage in the pouch category, but expressed confidence in its ability to lead the way over time. According to Mancuso, one of the main obstacles facing the industry is the widespread misconception that nicotine itself causes harm from tobacco use. Mancuso also highlighted the challenges posed by FDA regulations on his company's business, stating that responsibility must be at the forefront of everything Altria does in the nicotine sector. This emphasis on responsibility reflects the changing landscape of the tobacco industry and its growing focus on smoke-free products. Altria's lawsuit against the FDA is centered on the regulatory agency's review process for new tobacco products. The company claims that this process has become a major hurdle in getting its newer nicotine products to market. Specifically, Altria alleges that the FDA's evaluation of these products takes significantly longer than the 180-day deadline set by law. The Premarket Tobacco Product Application (PMTA) review process is a key point of contention between Altria and the FDA. Under this process, new tobacco products must undergo a thorough examination to determine whether they provide an overall public health benefit. However, Altria argues that the FDA's bureaucratic red tape has led to excessively long delays in reviewing these applications. Meanwhile, foreign competitors are flooding store shelves with their own nicotine products, often mislabeled as being made in the US. This not only erodes market share for legitimate companies but also allows illicit products to circumvent safety standards set by the FDA. Altria claims that this is a major concern and that enforcement against these illegal products is urgently needed. The issue of labeling is particularly problematic, with overseas products being marketed as made in the US when they are actually imported from countries like China. This misrepresentation can lead consumers to believe that these products meet stricter safety standards than they actually do. The FDA's failure to address this issue has created a regulatory vacuum that Altria is seeking to fill through its lawsuit. As part of its efforts to overhaul the PMTA review process, Altria is pushing for revisions to be made by the FDA. This includes streamlining the application process and reducing the time it takes for products to reach market. By doing so, Altria hopes to create a more level playing field for legitimate companies and reduce the proliferation of illicit nicotine products. The regulatory framework governing nicotine products is in dire need of reform, according to Altria's CEO, who believes that excessive information and lack of durability in guidelines hinder legitimate businesses from operating effectively. A more streamlined approach to regulation would allow companies like Altria to focus on delivering high-quality products while providing consumers with a wider range of choices. Rapid authorization processes would enable consumers to access various nicotine products without unnecessary delays or uncertainty. The regulatory landscape for cannabis in the US, where half of states have legalized it but lack federal standards, serves as a relevant example. This "hodgepodge" of regulations creates an uneven playing field that favors illicit operators over responsible businesses like Altria.
