articles.title: Salesforce Implements AI Spending Limits to Control Costs
articles.summary: The company's new policy allocates monthly token budgets for every role, allowing employees to focus their AI spend on high-priority tasks.
articles.content: Salesforce is taking steps to rein in its AI spending after some employees spent thousands of dollars per month on tokens last quarter. According to an internal memo viewed by this publication, the company's Chief Operating Officer Miguel Milano has implemented a new policy that allocates monthly token budgets for every role, allowing employees to focus their AI spend on high-priority tasks. The move reflects a common challenge faced by companies embracing AI technology - balancing cost control with employee empowerment. Other businesses have introduced similar spending limits in an effort to curb the rising costs of artificial intelligence. While Salesforce is setting AI budgets at the team level, rather than companywide, team leaders will be responsible for managing their groups' AI usage. The goal, as stated by a company spokesperson, is to ensure that AI investments deliver maximum impact for both business and customers. Salesforce has tested this new approach on one team with promising results, reporting that the group operated well under budget after just two months without any decline in productivity. The sales organization under President and Chief Revenue Officer Alexa Vignone will have a strict $1,000 monthly limit for technical roles, while non-technical employees like sellers are allocated just $100 per month for AI tokens. In contrast, the Customer Success team led by Jim Roth has a more modest budget of $500 per month for technical personnel, with non-technical staff receiving the same $100 allowance as their counterparts in other departments. Meanwhile, the Global Professional Services and Forward Deployed Engineering teams under Lori Steele are also subject to these new spending limits. Other companies have been experimenting with similar measures to control AI expenses, including Coinbase which has implemented weekly caps ranging from $500 to $5,000 based on employee roles and seniority. JPMorgan Chase, for instance, has introduced a monthly limit of $2,000 for some engineers using Anthropic's Claude Code. The company's CEO Marc Benioff had previously estimated that Salesforce would spend around $300 million on Anthropic tokens this year, primarily to develop coding agents. This new approach aims to focus AI spending on projects with the greatest impact for customers and the business, rather than simply encouraging adoption. To manage AI spending, Salesforce has introduced new budget limits for employees based on their roles within the company. Monthly token spend limits have been set at varying levels depending on an employee's role, with technical roles such as Alexa's Org Technical Roles allowed to spend up to $1,000 per month, while non-technical GTM/Seller Roles are capped at $100 per month. This new system aims to reduce the financial burden of AI spending, which had previously seen employees exceed their budgets by thousands of dollars each month. The company is now encouraging employees and their managers to work together to stay within allocated limits. As part of this initiative, leaders will be responsible for managing their team's budgets, much like they would with travel and entertainment expenses. The new AI budget guidelines specify that any request exceeding 3 times the individual limit will require approval from a more senior manager, namely Alexa, Jim, or Lori, who will also involve finance in the decision-making process. These higher-value requests are reviewed on a monthly basis to ensure they align with company goals and justify the additional expenditure through a clear return on investment justification. The increased budget will be valid for 90 days before being reassessed. This temporary allocation is intended to support ongoing projects, but it's not a long-term solution. A more comprehensive process is in development to better manage AI spend. As part of this interim setup, leaders are encouraged to track individual and team usage through the AI Spend Dashboard. They should review usage monthly to identify areas where costs can be optimized without compromising results. The memo advises employees to regularly review their AI budget usage to identify areas where costs can be optimized without sacrificing results. Visibility into pooled team spending will be provided for leaders in countries represented by the Works Council, allowing them to monitor and manage token allocation effectively. Gugerotti's trip took place on Tuesday, marking an important moment in the ongoing efforts to support Christian communities. Gugerotti prayed before the Holy Edicule inside the Church of the Holy Sepulcher, a site considered sacred by Christians as it marks where Jesus is believed to have been buried and resurrected. The cardinal's prayer was part of a solemn ceremony that brought together leaders from various Christian denominations in Jerusalem. Incense filled the air as clergy wore traditional robes, highlighting the importance of unity among the different faith groups. The unique arrangement of worship space in the basilica dates back to the 19th century and has sometimes led to tense interactions between the different Christian denominations. However, on this occasion, leaders from various backgrounds came together in a show of solidarity. Gugerotti's presence was accompanied by other Christian leaders, all of whom participated in the procession through Jerusalem's Old City. As they walked through the narrow stone alleyways, rows of Franciscan friars and a large cross preceded Gugerotti, creating a sense of grandeur and importance. The ceremony inside the centuries-old church offered a moment of hope for Christians in the region, who have been facing difficult times. A recent violent attack on a religious sister in April sent shockwaves across Israel, highlighting the vulnerability of those serving in the Holy Land. articles.title: Microbes thrive in toxic quarry environments
articles.summary: A geomicrobiologist is studying microbes at a quarry site to understand how they can contribute to addressing climate change.
articles.content: A quarry site may seem like an inhospitable environment, but appearances can be misleading. The barren landscape and exposed rock face hide millions of living microbes that thrive in conditions toxic to other life forms. Dr. Thomas Jones, a geomicrobiologist, has spent years studying these microorganisms at CSIRO, Australia's national science agency. His work focuses on identifying microbes already present in the quarry, which he then takes back to the lab for further research and experimentation. Jones's approach is to find existing microbial populations that can be used as starter cultures for his experiments. In other words, he seeks out microorganisms that are already adapted to their environment and could potentially contribute to addressing climate change. When collecting samples from the quarry site, Jones carefully gathers a small amount of material from the rock surface. This "smear may seem insignificant, but it holds great potential for understanding how microbes can be harnessed to mitigate environmental damage. The scale of microbial activity spans from the tiniest particles to the vast expanse of the planet itself. Geomicrobiologist Jones has spent his career studying the intricate relationships between microbes and minerals, seeking ways to harness these interactions for human benefit. Many of the processes he's studied have been crucial in shaping our planet over millions of years, with ancient microbial activities still influencing Earth's geology today. According to Jones, microbes have been removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere for an astonishing 3.5 billion years, a testament to their enduring impact on the environment. Stromatolites are a fascinating example of this phenomenon, formed by communities of photosynthetic microbes that extract carbon dioxide and lock it into calcium carbonate mineral layers, creating layered mounds that have been essential in producing Earth's early atmospheric oxygen. The intricate details of microbial interactions with minerals can be revealed using advanced imaging techniques such as scanning electron microscopes, which provide extraordinary surface detail. To further analyze the elemental composition of these samples, Jones employs X-ray fluorescence (XRF) mapping at ANSTO's Australian Synchrotron, allowing him to pinpoint specific elements within the mineral structures. For Jones, geomicrobiology is a creative pursuit that involves piecing together complex puzzles, much like painting a picture, he seeks to fill in gaps in understanding by identifying missing pieces of information that exist elsewhere. Microbes are ubiquitous and can thrive even in harsh environments such as neglected mine tailings dams, where water is highly acidic but still manage to survive. The pH scale is a crucial tool for measuring acidity, with pure water sitting at a neutral 7. But as one moves down the scale, each step becomes increasingly acidic, with lemon juice reaching a pH of 2 and stomach acid plummeting to around 1. In fact, some microbes can thrive in environments that would be hostile to most other forms of life, with acidity levels even dipping into negative numbers. This remarkable ability to adapt has left researchers like Jones in awe of the resilience of these tiny organisms. The sheer diversity and ubiquity of microbes have made them a valuable asset in the fight against climate change. By harnessing their power, scientists are discovering new ways to mitigate the effects of global warming. One such process is enhanced rock weathering, which involves crushing up basalt, a type of gray rock commonly used in road gravel and building sites, and spreading it across farmland. As the rock breaks down, it releases essential minerals that help lock carbon dioxide out of the air while neutralizing soil acidity. By accelerating this natural process, researchers aim to create a more stable form of carbon storage that can help combat climate change. Field trips by Jones yield diverse microbial communities that are more resilient to changing environments than lab-grown strains. These broad communities are then adjusted through careful manipulation of nutrients and acidity, allowing a specific group to flourish. Once an optimal mix is achieved, it's dubbed gold" in microbe form - the "Daddy consortium". This potent blend of microbes is now ready for deployment in the field. However, things don't always go according to plan when introducing these microbes into complex ecosystems like soil. Pure cultures accustomed to laboratory environments can struggle to adapt and may be outcompeted by established microbial populations. Every microbe in a given environment plays a vital role and has evolved to thrive under specific conditions, leaving little room for newcomers. Jones acknowledges that working on farms adds an extra layer of complexity due to the delicate balance already present. Any changes to soil chemistry could disrupt this equilibrium and undermine the efforts put into maintaining the farm's ecosystem. Jones must therefore be mindful of his approach when introducing microbes to these environments. When working with farms, timing is a crucial factor in deploying rock dust and microbes effectively. Applying them just after rain allows the microbes to settle and establish themselves before being washed away. Conversely, spreading them out just before the onset of the wet season enables them to be carried into the soil where they can take hold. Throughout this process, Jones remains acutely aware that he's working with living organisms that require careful consideration and handling. His approach must strike a balance between introducing beneficial microbes while respecting the existing ecosystem and minimizing potential disruptions. To succeed in enlisting microbes to combat climate change, it's essential that they are content and able to thrive in their new environment. This requires a delicate balance between providing them with what they need to function effectively and not overstimulating them. Jones' background is in geology, but he discovered his passion for microbiology through elective courses in college. It was there that he became aware of the vast potential of microbes to be harnessed for beneficial purposes. This epiphany marked a significant turning point in his academic and professional journey. The XXXX brewery in Brisbane proved to be an unexpected yet valuable source of starter cultures for Jones' early research. He has always been drawn to novel and unconventional approaches, which has served him well in his work as a microbiologist. His enthusiasm for the field is evident in his comments about its vast potential. Jones' professional path has taken him on a global journey, with stops in Australia, Brazil, and southern Africa. Along the way, he completed his Ph.D. at the University of Queensland and successfully scaled up microbial techniques from laboratory settings to industry applications. This experience has provided him with a unique perspective on the practical applications of microbiology. The work being conducted by Jones and his team is focused on developing mineral-building microbes that can store carbon for extended periods in Western Australia. In this context, he is collaborating with some of the oldest and most effective carbon catchers on Earth, the microbes themselves. He has a straightforward approach when working with these tiny helpers - he simply asks them to take on the task of capturing carbon from the atmosphere. The microbes are a massive team effort, comprising the vast majority of Earth's inhabitants, and most of them remain invisible to the naked eye. articles.title: Groundbreaking Discovery Made in Astrophysics Using NSF VLBA
articles.summary: A team led by Paul Boven made a surprising discovery that both stars in DG CVn emit detectable radio waves, allowing astronomers to track their individual motions with remarkable accuracy.
articles.content: Astronomers have made a groundbreaking discovery in the field of astrophysics by measuring the orbit, masses, and distance of a pair of small, active stars with unprecedented precision. The observations were made using the U.S. National Science Foundation's Very Long Baseline Array (NSF VLBA), operated by the National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO). This binary system, known as DG CVn, is located approximately 59 light-years from Earth and consists of two red dwarf stars that orbit each other. A team led by Paul Boven, a network system engineer at the Joint Institute for Very Long Baseline Interferometry ERIC (JIVE), made the surprising discovery that both stars in DG CVn emit detectable radio waves. This allowed astronomers to track their individual motions across the sky with remarkable accuracy. The observations provide a detailed picture of this binary system, which is still relatively young, estimated to be between 30 and 150 million years old. DG CVn is an interesting case study for astronomers because it consists of two red dwarf stars that exhibit intense activity. When these stars rotate rapidly, they generate powerful magnetic fields and intense flares that produce strong radio and X-ray emission. This makes them a rare and fascinating subject of study in the field of astrophysics. The observations were made over an 18-year period, including new data collected between 2023 and 2025 using the NSF VLBA. By combining this data with previous observations, the team was able to determine the stars' orbit and masses with unusual accuracy. This achievement is a testament to the power of long-term observations in astronomy. The study's lead author, Paul Boven, is a Ph.D. student at Leiden Observatory and a network system engineer at JIVE. His team's work provides valuable insights into the behavior of red dwarf stars and their potential for intense activity. The findings have been published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics, offering a new perspective on this fascinating binary system. Further research is needed to understand the complex dynamics of DG CVn and its implications for our understanding of star formation and evolution. The study's results also highlight the importance of continued observations using advanced astronomical instruments like the NSF VLBA. The system's radio emission has been found to surge dramatically following powerful X-ray outbursts, leaving astronomers with a pressing question: which star is responsible for this phenomenon? The researchers' initial observations of DG CVn were motivated by a search for planets around nearby stars. However, the system's behavior proved far more complex than anticipated, exhibiting large and unpredictable motion that defied explanation. We were fortunate to have developed the necessary tools to interpret these motions, said Boven, but the real surprise came when we detected a second radio-loud dwarf during our confirmation observations. The team combined archival data from 2007-2010 with seven new observing sessions between 2023 and 2025 to produce 27 precise measurements of the system's two stars. The team used the NSF VLBA's unique capability to combine the signals from its 10 radio telescopes across North America into a single, highly sensitive instrument. This allowed them to pinpoint the locations of the radio emission from each star with unprecedented precision. DG CVn is an exemplary case of what can be achieved through precise radio astrometry, according to Jay Blanchard, an astronomer at the NSF NRAO and co-author on the study. By tracking the two stars over many years, researchers can observe their orbital motion directly and use that information to determine properties that would otherwise be extremely challenging to measure. The observations revealed that the two stars orbit each other once every 4.511 years in a stretched, elliptical path. At their closest approach, they come within about 0.59 times the average distance between Earth and the sun. DG CVn A is significantly more massive than DG CVn B, with approximately 39% of the sun's mass, while its companion has roughly 36%. These masses were determined using data from the team's observations. The system is relatively close to Earth, situated at a distance of about 59.3 light-years away. Researchers employed a technique called parallax to calculate this distance by measuring the tiny apparent shift in the position of DG CVn as Earth moves around the sun. Knowing both the system's distance and the way the two stars move around each other enabled the researchers to calculate their masses with exceptional accuracy, providing one of the most precise dynamical measurements yet for a binary system of this type. The gravitational interactions between two stars in a binary system can have far-reaching consequences for their planetary systems. The close proximity of the stars in DG CVn, just 0.59 astronomical units apart, would have limited the size of the gas and dust disks surrounding each star as they formed. This limitation likely had an impact on the formation of planets around these stars. To remain stable, a planet orbiting one of the stars would need to complete its orbit in under 23 days. Conversely, a planet that orbited both stars would require a much longer orbital period, lasting at least 36 years. The constraints on planetary orbits imposed by the binary system provide valuable insights into how such systems can influence the formation and survival of planets. The close encounters between the two stars may have also played a role in shaping their planetary systems. VLBI, or very long baseline interferometry, proved to be an essential tool for this research. By combining radio telescopes over vast distances, researchers were able to make extremely precise measurements of the binary system's position and motion. The exceptional precision achieved through VLBI enabled the researchers to calculate the masses of the stars with great accuracy. This achievement highlights the power of advanced astronomical techniques in unlocking the secrets of celestial systems. Measuring the tiny motion caused by an orbiting planet can be a key indicator of its presence. As a planet travels around its star, it creates a slight "reflex" motion that can be detected using sophisticated instruments like those employed in this study. The study suggests that future radio telescopes could greatly expand our ability to measure the properties of binary star systems. These new facilities will enable astronomers to detect the subtle effects caused by binary companions and distinguish them from planets orbiting nearby stars. By achieving such precision, scientists can gain a better understanding of how these systems behave and interact with their environment. The ngVLA and SKA will be able to make precise measurements for many more distant stars. The team hopes that future observations will allow them to detect planets in orbit around radio-loud dwarf stars, providing valuable insights into the formation and evolution of planetary systems. articles.title: Radiation Damage to Electronic Devices Studied in Experiment
articles.summary: Researchers at North Carolina State University have made progress in understanding how radiation damages electronic devices.
articles.content: A team of researchers has made significant progress in understanding how radiation damages electronic devices, a crucial step towards developing more resilient electronics for use in extreme environments. In an experiment that pushed the limits of human endurance, Cristyan Quiñones at North Carolina State University spent nearly three days monitoring a beam of heavy ions as it destroyed an array of electronic devices. The high-stakes research aimed to provide valuable insights into the effects of radiation on electronics. The researchers focused their attention on a particular type of semiconductor called aluminium nitride, made from aluminium and nitrogen, which is used in electronics components known as diodes. These components are vital for powering electronic devices and have been touted as a promising foundation for future generations of power components. Aluminium nitride was initially thought to be resistant to radiation exposure, making it an attractive choice for use in high-radiation environments such as space or near nuclear reactors. However, the experiment revealed that even this seemingly resilient material is vulnerable to the effects of radiation. The team's findings bring them one step closer to understanding the phenomenon known as "single-event burnout" (SEB), where electronic devices rapidly fail due to radiation exposure. By systematically studying this process, the researchers hope to develop more robust electronics capable of withstanding extreme radiation levels. The process of Single Event Burnout (SEB) has long been a concern for electronic devices used in space, but researchers have yet to thoroughly investigate its effects in experiments. A recent study, conducted by a team of scientists at North Carolina State University and NASA, aimed to fill this knowledge gap. The experiment involved bombarding aluminium nitride diodes with energetic ions from silver, gold, or the rare earth metal praseodymium. These ions caused disturbances within the diode's structure, which combined with the applied voltage created a localized electric field. At some threshold voltage, this field became strong enough to trigger an avalanche of electrons onto a small area, leading to a miniature explosion. Microscopic images from the experiment revealed tiny craters on the surface of the aluminium nitride diodes where SEB had occurred, further supporting the team's conclusions about the mechanism behind this phenomenon. Power systems on spacecrafts are often the most susceptible to damage from space radiation, and even physical shields may not be enough to protect electronics from phenomena like Single Event Burnout (SEB). According to Schrimpf, studying materials that could potentially withstand such radiation is crucial for the development of more resilient power devices. This research has far-reaching implications beyond space exploration, as it can also inform the design of electronics used in nuclear engineering and radiation therapy. The scarcity of facilities for testing electronics materials, such as ion beams like the one used in this experiment, adds to the complexity of making electronics ready for space. However, understanding the physical processes behind SEB is key to innovation in this area, says Collazo. By uncovering the physics behind electron avalanches in aluminium nitride, researchers can now design devices that take into account these specific vulnerabilities and develop principles for more resilient electronic systems. articles.title: Flock Safety Cameras Found in Public Spaces Across US
articles.summary: Flock Safety cameras are often overlooked despite their widespread presence in public areas.
articles.content: Flock cameras have become ubiquitous in public spaces, but their presence often goes unnoticed. Their capabilities and potential uses far exceed what most people assume they can do. The automated license plate reader (ALPR) version is perhaps the most well-known type, typically mounted on a pole with a solar panel attached for power. However, Flock Safety's product has become synonymous with ALPR cameras, despite there being numerous other manufacturers and vendors offering similar technology. These alternative products often have distinct designs but serve essentially the same purpose: reading license plates and recording vehicle activity. Most of these devices are small, roughly hand-sized, and have a vertically oval shape, making them easy to miss in their surroundings. A solar panel is frequently attached to provide power, ensuring continuous operation without interruption. The appearance of ALPR cameras can vary significantly depending on the manufacturer, with some notable examples being those made by Leonardo and Genetec. Flock cameras blend in seamlessly with their surroundings, making them easily mistaken for standard traffic cameras or vice versa. This blurring of lines creates a challenge for projects like DeFlock, which relies on volunteers to visually identify Flock cameras. The capabilities of Flock cameras extend beyond automatic license plate recognition (ALPRs). Depending on the customer's requirements, the system can capture additional details such as roof racks on vehicles and bumper stickers. Some setups even come equipped with microphones, while others can recognize specific clothing items or facial features like beards. Flock cameras are typically deployed in high-traffic areas where roads converge, often mounted on poles at busy intersections or neighborhood entrances. Given the significant presence of homeowners associations (HOAs) among Flock's customer base, it's not surprising to find them at these locations. Shopping centers also represent potential sites for Flock camera installations. When attempting to identify a Flock camera, its orientation is an important consideration. Since the primary purpose is to capture license plates, the camera should be angled accordingly. A telltale sign of a Flock camera is the presence of the company's bird logo on the device and a solar panel above it, typically indicating self-sufficiency. The lack of additional equipment nearby often serves as another indicator that a camera is a Flock model. In contrast to red light and speed cameras, which are usually larger and connected to traffic signals or enforcement poles, Flock cameras tend to be more discreet. Flock cameras come in various forms, not all of which are immediately recognizable as such. The company offers a range of products, including the Condor, a spherical camera that can rotate 360 degrees to track individuals. This particular model is typically mounted near high-traffic areas where pedestrians congregate. However, Flock's product line extends beyond fixed installations, also encompassing mobile security trailers and gunshot detection systems. The company has even explored drone-based solutions for emergency response situations. As a result of this proliferation of different products, it may become increasingly challenging to identify a Flock camera or one similar in design. This can be attributed to the growing trend of repurposing standard IP cameras as plate readers using video integration tools. Consequently, users will need to rely on more comprehensive resources to determine whether law enforcement agencies are utilizing such technology in their area. A useful starting point for this inquiry is the Atlas of Surveillance, a searchable database maintained by the Electronic Frontier Foundation that catalogues the surveillance technologies employed by various law enforcement agencies. To uncover the presence of Flock cameras in your area, it's essential to be proactive in seeking out information. Submitting a public records request is one effective way to obtain this data, allowing you to access detailed information about these surveillance systems. A more hands-on approach involves attending local council meetings or asking business owners and homeowners' associations directly if they are aware of any Flock cameras in the area. articles.content: General Motors President Mark Reuss asserted his confidence in Detroit's automotive industry at the F500 Innovation Forum, stating "I'm not afraid of Chinese cars." However, he also acknowledged that GM is closely monitoring China's rapidly growing manufacturing sector. China has set a remarkable record for auto exports, shipping over 8 million passenger vehicles during the first 10 months of 2026. To counter this trend, Reuss highlighted the strengths of Detroit's GM factories, emphasizing their capacity to produce high-quality vehicles at scale. Reuss' comments were made during a panel discussion with Fortune's Executive Editor Lee Clifford, where he showcased GM's expertise in critical areas such as safety, durability, and long-term reliability. He also emphasized the importance of design, stating "aesthetic design is an essential aspect of the company's products. The stakes are high for American workers, who make up a significant portion of the motor vehicles and component parts sector. According to the Department of Energy, this industry employed around 2.6 million U.S. workers in 2025, a decrease of over 50,000 from the previous year. Reuss pointed to GM's factories as a key competitive advantage, citing their ability to produce at scale and maintain a large workforce. He also emphasized the importance of talent, stating our people are second to none and asserting that GM has the best automotive expertise in the country. GM's president, Reuss, emphasized that the company has been studying its competitors in China since 1984, having operated there for nearly four decades. This experience has given them a deep understanding of Chinese cars and their capabilities. As he noted, We know Chinese cars, which suggests that GM is well-positioned to compete with its Chinese rivals. GM's approach to staying ahead of the competition involves not just studying its local competitors but also those from around the world. According to Reuss, the company disassembles rival vehicles to gain insights into their design and technology. This hands-on approach allows them to learn from others and adapt their own strategies accordingly. As he quipped, Only the paranoid survive, right? China's auto export growth has been nothing short of remarkable, with the country shipping over eight million passenger vehicles in the first ten months of 2026 alone. In October, exports reached a staggering 927,000 units, representing a 62.3% increase from the previous year. This surge is part of an already record-breaking year for Chinese auto exports. China's electric vehicle production has been driving much of this growth, with the country accounting for nearly three-quarters of global EV production in 2025. That year, China produced around 16 million electric cars, and its exports more than doubled to a record 2.5 million vehicles. These figures represent over one-third of all Chinese vehicle exports and demonstrate the significant role that electric vehicles are playing in driving the country's auto export boom. The automotive sector plays a significant role in the US manufacturing base, supporting millions of jobs across various industries including factories, suppliers, distribution networks, and repair businesses. According to a report by the Congressional Research Service released in March 2026, the automotive industry accounts for approximately 4.8% of the country's GDP and supports around 10.1 million direct and indirect employment opportunities. This sector is crucial to the US economy, providing a substantial contribution to its overall growth. General Motors has been working on making its vehicles more affordable by pricing six models at around $30,000, with over 600,000 units sold so far this year following nearly one million last year. The company's president emphasized that achieving profitability in such a competitive market is challenging but they are committed to succeeding. GM learned the hard way that cutting costs alone cannot solve problems; instead, the company went through several reorganizations, downsizing, and consolidations over the years. This experience culminated in the company filing for bankruptcy in 2009, with its president noting that nothing happens until you sell a car." GM's domestic manufacturing footprint is being strengthened through significant investments in supply chains, production capacity, and final assembly facilities within the US. This move aims to bolster America's ability to manufacture vehicles and technology, which Reuss believes is crucial for its long-term competitive success. He emphasizes that bringing industrial might and jobs back into the country will have a profound impact on its economic landscape. Reuss advocates for a single national rulebook instead of state-by-state regulation, citing the billions of dollars wasted by the industry trying to comply with individual state regulations rather than a consistent nationwide set of rules. The demand for gas-powered engines remains high and is expected to persist in the coming years. articles.title: Mice Invade Homes Through Hidden Food Sources
articles.summary: A common problem for households is the sudden appearance of mysterious droppings or debris under furniture, which can be a sign of unwanted visitors.
articles.content: Mice are notorious for invading homes, often seeking out food sources in unexpected places. A common hiding spot is the bedroom, where they can feast on crumbs and spills left behind by residents. According to eyewitness accounts, a rustling sound from the wastebasket can be an early warning sign of unwanted visitors. The sudden appearance of mysterious droppings or debris under furniture can send shockwaves through even the most vigilant household members. One resident recounts shining their phone flashlight down the back of a piece of furniture only to discover chocolate-covered raisins, not mouse droppings as initially feared. Food waste and clutter can make a bedroom an appealing destination for mice and rats. Crumbs, discarded packaging, and uneaten snacks provide a feast for these unwanted visitors. According to Adam Hart, professor of conservation ecology at the University of Gloucestershire, food is a primary draw for rodents. Dirty laundry and personal items can also serve as nesting material for mice. In fact, Adam notes that these attractants are more about providing shelter and potential nesting sites once rodents have entered the room rather than drawing them in initially. Dirty plates and glasses, like those found hidden under a bed, can be a sign of a larger issue. Keeping food out of the bedroom is crucial to resolving this problem. It's also essential to maintain a tidy space by regularly cleaning up clutter and doing laundry. Mice are notorious for seeking out materials to build their nests, often shredding paper and cardboard to create a cozy habitat. Dark and undisturbed areas with low traffic are prime targets for these rodents, making the bottom of your wardrobe or chest of drawers a potential hotspot. Rodents require water to survive, but they don't need much, which is good news for households. Adam notes that while condensation itself may not be a major draw for mice, leaks and readily available water can help sustain them. Moisture levels play a significant role in attracting mice into your bedroom. Since rats require more water than mice, condensation alone is unlikely to draw them in. Instead, mice may seek out leaky pipes or other sources of water in the en suite if it's conveniently located. To eliminate humidity as an attractant, consider ventilating the bedroom by opening windows and doors, or using a dehumidifier to reduce moisture levels. This simple step can help make your home less appealing to unwanted visitors. Cracks and gaps around windows and doors are just the beginning when it comes to potential entry points for unwanted visitors. Seal up holes with caulk and reinforce with steel wool to prevent rodents from squeezing through even the tiniest openings. Look out for vulnerable areas along skirting boards, in attics via the roofline, and anywhere else that might provide a mouse-sized gap. Identifying how these pests are getting into your home is crucial to effective prevention, and experts agree that addressing this first step can make all the difference in keeping them out. By taking care of the obvious entrances, you'll be well on your way to creating an inhospitable environment for mice. articles.title: England's NEET Crisis Affects Almost 1 Million Young People Between Ages 16-24
articles.summary: A landmark review by Alan Milburn has led to Prime Minister Andy Burnham adopting a "whole-childhood approach" to prevent young people from becoming NEET.
articles.content: Almost 1 million young people in England between the ages of 16 and 24 are not in education, employment, or training, sparking concerns about the country's NEET crisis. In response to a landmark review on this issue by Alan Milburn, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has vowed to adopt a "whole-childhood approach" aimed at preventing young people from falling through the cracks. This means providing support to those with specific needs and vulnerabilities. Research shows that poverty, poor mental health, and special education needs or disabilities are common among NEET individuals. However, even when multiple risk factors are present in two young people, their paths can diverge significantly, with one moving into further education or employment while the other becomes NEET. Despite being able to identify patterns of disadvantage through data analysis, there's a significant gap between understanding which young people are at risk and knowing what contributes to them becoming or remaining NEET. The distinction between identifying risk and understanding pathways to becoming NEET is crucial for effective policy-making. While researchers have made significant progress in pinpointing which young people are most likely to end up not in education, employment, or training (NEET), the underlying reasons remain shrouded in mystery. Our team reviewed 861 records and identified 36 relevant data sets that shed light on NEET levels among 16- to 24-year-olds in England. These data sets include national studies like the Millennium Cohort Study and large household surveys such as Understanding Society, which provide a comprehensive picture of young people's circumstances and outcomes. In addition to these studies, we also examined records from schools, government departments, and other public services that collect data on young people's lives over time. While only four of the 36 identified data sets measured NEET status directly, others included valuable information about groups at greater risk of becoming NEET and how their lives changed over time. The available data offer a nuanced understanding of patterns and characteristics that help policymakers identify who may require additional support. However, our review revealed a significant gap: while data can pinpoint which young people are at risk of becoming NEET, they often fail to explain why individuals' pathways diverge in the first place. A typical data set might reveal correlations between school absence and disengagement from education, employment, or training, but it usually cannot provide insight into what happens between those two points in time. This gap highlights a critical challenge for policymakers seeking to address the NEET problem effectively. Administrative records often fall short in answering crucial questions about a young person's life. For instance, were their support needs recognized and addressed during a critical transition period? The lack of information on these matters hinders policymakers' efforts to address the NEET problem effectively. Our previous research has shown that accessing linked administrative data is a significant challenge. This gap highlights the limitations of relying solely on administrative records to understand the complexities of youth transitions. Young people with special education needs and disabilities (Send) are around twice as likely to become NEET as those without such needs, according to our analysis. The presence of childhood poverty further exacerbates this risk. Among young men eligible for free school meals due to their family's low income and also having a Send record, nearly one in four were NEET, compared with fewer than one in 14 among those with neither characteristic. Analyzing youth disengagement in England is a complex task that requires more than just identifying at-risk groups. One key challenge is understanding the context surrounding these young people's experiences. Administrative records can provide valuable insights into patterns and trends, but they often fail to capture the intricate web of factors influencing an individual's path. Young people's own perspectives are crucial in filling this knowledge gap. Through interviews, participatory research, and accessible surveys, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of how educational experiences, local opportunities, family responsibilities, and support systems interact. This approach allows for a more nuanced understanding of the challenges faced by young people. The government-commissioned review on youth unemployment highlights the importance of shifting the narrative away from individual failing. The research suggests that even when we identify high-risk groups, we may not have the evidence needed to understand where support breaks down and what works in these situations. This gap in knowledge hinders the development of effective strategies for addressing youth disengagement. A coordinated system tackling youth disengagement must move beyond mere identification of at-risk individuals. It demands a deeper understanding of the barriers young people encounter, as well as the support that helps them transition towards education, training, or employment. This requires learning from their experiences and using this knowledge to inform policy decisions. Effective interventions rely on more than just administrative data; they also require an empathetic understanding of the challenges faced by young people. By prioritizing these perspectives and experiences, policymakers can develop targeted strategies that address the root causes of youth disengagement, rather than just its symptoms. By analyzing administrative and research data, England has been able to identify which young people are at risk of becoming Not in Education, Employment, or Training (NEET). However, this information does not provide a clear understanding of why these individuals are more likely to be NEET. To address the root causes of youth disengagement, policymakers need to go beyond just identifying the problem. This involves considering various factors that may contribute to a young person's likelihood of becoming NEET. As Lombardo et al. point out in their research, administrative and research data can only provide part of the picture, and other perspectives are essential for developing effective strategies. Understanding why certain groups of young people are more likely to be NEET is crucial for policymakers to develop targeted interventions that address the underlying causes of disengagement. By prioritizing these perspectives and experiences, policymakers can create a more comprehensive approach to addressing youth disengagement, ultimately helping to reduce the number of young people who become NEET in England. articles.title: EU and ASEAN Mark 50 Years of Diplomatic Ties Amid Trade Agreement Progress
articles.summary: The European Union and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations are marking 50 years of diplomatic ties with significant developments in their trade relations.
articles.content: The European Union and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) are on the cusp of significant developments in their trade relations, as they mark 50 years of diplomatic ties next year. A major milestone will be the implementation of a long-awaited trade agreement with Indonesia, while negotiations with Thailand and Malaysia are gaining momentum. The EU is also close to finalizing a deal with the Philippines, which could bring the number of Southeast Asian states with which it has trade agreements up from just two today to six by the end of next year. The anniversary of their diplomatic ties may also revive the long-held ambition of a broader trade agreement between the EU and ASEAN. This would represent a significant step forward in their economic cooperation, but several challenges must first be overcome. On November 17, the European Commission hosted a dialogue in Brussels to discuss trade relations with Southeast Asia, where progress on existing and pending free trade agreements (FTAs) was assessed. The European Union's push for deeper trade ties with Southeast Asia has made significant progress in recent years, but experts warn that informal barriers to commerce still pose a major challenge. To truly succeed, free trade agreements (FTAs) need to address not only formal regulations, but also the unwritten rules and local practices that can be just as daunting for European businesses. For instance, European companies with limited experience in Southeast Asia would greatly benefit from on-the-ground support, particularly practical guidance on navigating informal business customs and local regulations. This could involve expanding assistance offered by European chambers of commerce, trade delegations, and EU offices in the region to help firms find distributors, explain licensing requirements, and qualify for preferential tariffs. Regular consultations between Brussels and businesses in Southeast Asia could help identify potential trade issues early on, preventing them from escalating into full-blown disputes. The EU's trade policy has taken on a new dimension, driven by a desire to reduce strategic dependencies. According to Nessel, this means setting clear objectives for trade policy, which is currently lacking. One area of concern is the EU's reliance on a small number of suppliers for critical minerals used in clean technologies. Southeast Asian producers, such as Indonesia, want foreign investors to help develop domestic processing industries rather than simply exporting raw materials. The EU and Indonesia have already clashed over Jakarta's restrictions on nickel exports. European investment in processing facilities, environmental agreements, and regulatory clarity would provide tangible benefits to both sides. Nessel emphasized that the true value of a free trade agreement lies not only in opening up new markets but also in giving the EU leverage to maintain access to those markets. The European Union is reevaluating its approach to trade agreements in Southeast Asia, a region where informal barriers often hinder business operations. Indonesia's decision to terminate bilateral investment treaties with several EU countries, including the Netherlands and Spain, has sparked concerns about the lack of legal protections for investors in the country. This development highlights the need for clearer guidelines on investments in Indonesia, a key player in Southeast Asia. The EU is reassessing its strategy for trade agreements in ASEAN, considering whether to pursue bilateral deals or revive its original ambition of a region-to-region agreement with ASEAN. ASEAN has already established regional free trade agreements with several economies, including China, which upgraded its deal with the bloc in October 2025. This development underscores the complexity of the EU's efforts to establish deeper ties with ASEAN through trade agreements. The EU-ASEAN Business Council is advocating for negotiations on a region-to-region Digital Trade Agreement and Investment Protection Agreement, citing the need for common approaches to customs procedures, supply-chain standards, and green technologies. According to Hakeem Jeffries, the likely speaker of the House, Democrats should capitalize on their "historic majority in the lower chamber and robust majority in the upper one to drive significant healthcare reforms. Jeffries' proposals go beyond his pre-election agenda, which focused on reversing Medicaid spending cuts and restoring expired tax credits under the Affordable Care Act. Jeffries emphasized the need for Congress to take swift action on healthcare reform, pushing beyond his pre-election agenda's focus on reversing Medicaid cuts and restoring expired tax credits under the Affordable Care Act. He expressed a desire to tackle long-standing issues in the medical field, including funding research for pediatric cancer, as part of a broader effort to address the nation's healthcare woes. The Democratic leader acknowledged that merely returning to the status quo is not an acceptable solution. The party's potential gains in Congress could pave the way for more ambitious legislation, with estimates suggesting Democrats may secure 259 House seats and 56 Senate seats after the elections, including a likely win in Alaska. As Democrats anticipate significant gains in Congress, party leaders are already planning their legislative agenda. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries emphasized the importance of coordination between the two chambers, stating that our two respective caucuses are going to have to work their will in conversation with each other to achieve their goals. Notably, key committee chairs will play a crucial role in shaping this legislation. Senator Bernie Sanders, chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, will be instrumental in negotiations. Known as the OG from Brooklyn, Sanders is a leading champion of Medicare for All, which he believes would make significant progress if implemented. Senator Sanders praised Jeffries' approach, noting that it aligns with his own proposal's first-year objectives. This includes lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 55 and extending benefits while covering all children. According to Senator Sanders, Medicare for All is a four-year transition program," and Jeffries' plan would represent significant progress towards this goal. articles.title: Chrome Update Released on Googlebook OS with New Features
articles.summary: The update introduces several performance enhancements and new features designed to streamline user workflow and browsing experience.
articles.content: Google has released an update for its Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, bringing new features and performance enhancements to streamline user workflow and browsing experience. Mixed reviews have greeted the first batch of Googlebooks hitting the market, but this update may just be what these laptops need to gain more functionality in Chrome comparable to other browsers. One of the key updates is a tab-sharing feature that should make video calls easier. When sharing a browser tab during a call, users will now see a control bar at the top of the window allowing them to stop sharing or switch tabs without having to start and stop repeatedly. The update also includes an improved vertical tab rail system: hover over it with your mouse or trackpad and the collapsed rail will expand, displaying full tab titles and enabling easier switching between tabs. The latest Chrome update has introduced a range of new features designed to enhance user experience and productivity. One notable improvement is the auto-expand feature for vertical tabs, which is enabled by default but can be toggled on or off in Settings. To customize your tab layout, you can now manually resize the vertical tab bar to display longer page titles when needed. This will also allow the browser to remember your preferred tab width even after opening a new window or restarting Chrome. The only prerequisite for this feature is disabling auto-expand tabs on hover. A significant time-saving innovation in the update allows users to save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses, which can be bookmarked, linked to, or accessed directly via their URL. This eliminates the need to navigate through menus to access frequently used settings pages. The updated system also enables users to switch between these saved settings pages using standard navigation buttons. The update has also improved the file saving process by enabling the "Save As" file picker for menu actions such as saving links or images. This allows users to easily rename files and select a destination folder, including options like Google Drive or external storage devices. In addition to these new features, Chrome M157 includes several performance enhancements aimed at improving overall browsing speed. These include the ability to quickly reveal web addresses using Ctrl+L, keeping bookmarks visible while sharing screens, enhanced media controls in Picture-in-Picture mode, and partial PDF translation capabilities within the browser itself. The latest Chrome update brings a range of new features and performance improvements to users who have their browser set up for automatic updates. This means that those who rely on the browser's default settings won't need to take any action to enjoy the benefits of the update. However, users who have disabled automatic updates can still install the update manually by accessing Chrome's Help menu, where they'll find an option to relaunch the browser with the new version. If this option is greyed out or missing entirely, it's likely that Chrome has already been updated to its latest iteration. The update also ensures a seamless experience for users who were working on tasks before the update took place, as Chrome will automatically save open tabs and reopen them when the user restarts their browser.
